correctness.rationale: The padded-word parity transform has exactly r=n-2k+1 flips; a size-r+1 prescribed alternating trace with fixed endpoints needs r+2 flips, proving the defect upper bound, while cardinality gives the k bound. Explicit pairs at q_i=3i-2 with spaced fillers realize every labeling of t=min(k,r) queries. The standard shift bijection counts the class as binomial(k+r,r); leaf counting and the all-positive branch yield its online upper bounds. Separating r blocks of size 2b_i by zero positions realizes a direct product of b_i+1-point threshold families, giving the online lower bound and the exact r=1/r>=k boundaries. For fixed r the bounds agree in coefficient r of log2 k. The separate checker exhaustively verifies VC for 70 (n,k) cases through n=14, every gadget labeling through n=21, and recursively computes Ldim through n=13; infinite statements are proved, not inferred from tests.

value.rationale: The exact-cardinality independence model is naturally motivated by graph independent-set enumeration and constrained binary words. Its VC capacity changes at the near-maximum-packing defect r and is exactly min(k,r) for all parameters; this is not a textbook rank for unrestricted independent sets. The same family has online dimension growing as r log2 k with sharp leading coefficient at each fixed positive defect, despite constant VC dimension, and the one-defect and high-slack endpoints have exact online formulas. This supplies a substantive structural learning-theoretic separation for a canonical constrained set family, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
